title: onprem/airgap: offline bundle vendor updates for rke2 + AlmaLinux 9 package refresh and rollback tooling
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes:
- Add rke2/almalinux9 vendor bundle and package refresh for on-prem air-gapped installer.
- Include new rollback helper scripts to revert TUF/apt metadata and container artifacts.
- Update Helm charts and Terraform module docs to expose vendor selection and mirror configuration.
description:
Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped environments requested official support for AlmaLinux 9 as a vendored OS image for rke2-based installs, plus improved rollback tooling for TUF/apt mirror updates. This PR assembles the offline bundle, refreshes vendor packages for rke2 on AlmaLinux 9, and adds a small rollback toolkit to safely revert metadata if bundle application fails.

What this changes (single-continuous description):
- Add vendor/almalinux9/ directory containing: pre-seeded RPM repo, patched rke2 systemd unit, curated container images (OCI tarballs), and TUF metadata packaged for offline use.
- Update onprem-installer/chart/values.yaml and charts/redwood/templates to add vendorSelector and mirrorConfig options, with backwards-compatible defaults.
- Terraform: expose new variable vendor_os and mirror_endpoint in modules/private-installer to let customers preconfigure onprem mirror sync.
- Add scripts/tools/rollback/README.md and scripts/tools/rollback/revert_tuf.sh (idempotent, dry-run capable) plus a containerized helper to restore apt/yum metadata and container image indexes from the previous bundle snapshot.
- Update docs/site/onprem/airgap.md with vendor selection examples and recommended validation checks after bundle apply.

Checklist: 
- [x] Offline bundle built and smoke-tested in lab (rke2 on AlmaLinux 9 VM).
- [x] Rollback scripts tested against simulated TUF metadata corruption.
- [x] Helm chart default values kept backwards-compatible.
- [x] Terraform variables added with clear documentation.
- [x] Added unit tests for installer validation step that checks bundle manifest integrity.

Commits (summary):
- vendor(almalinux9): add packaged RPM repo and rke2 bits
- infra(installer): expose vendor/mirror vars in terraform module
- charts(onprem-installer): add vendorSelector + mirrorConfig defaults
- tooling(rollback): add revert_tuf.sh and container helper + README
- docs: airgap vendor selection and validation guidance

Files changed (high-level):
- vendor/almalinux9/* (RPMs, container tarballs, tuf metadata)
- onprem-installer/chart/values.yaml, onprem-installer/chart/templates/*
- terraform/modules/private-installer/variables.tf, outputs.tf, README.md
- scripts/tools/rollback/revert_tuf.sh, rollback_helper/Dockerfile, rollback/README.md
- docs/site/onprem/airgap.md
- tests/installer/test_bundle_manifest.py

Testing: bundle was applied to a lab cluster (rke2 v1.25 on AlmaLinux 9) behind simulated NAT/mirror. Smoke tests: cluster join, basic pod e2e, image pull from local mirror. Rollback tests: simulated missing TUF targets -> revert_tuf.sh restored previous metadata and cluster recovered image pulls. CI: initial pipeline failed due to linting in revert_tuf.sh (shebang/permissions), fixed on second push; final CI green (unit tests + integration smoke).

Review conversation summary: 
- Miguel Sanchez (reviewer): "Main concerns are bundle size (we should avoid shipping dev-only images) and ensuring the Terraform variable names are consistent with other modules."
  - Author (Aisha Patel): "Dropped ~30 dev/test images from the bundle (now ~2.1GB reduced) and renamed variable vendor_os -> vendor_os (kept same but clarified in README) to avoid drift. Confirmed with infra team."
- Priya Menon (security): "Audit of RPMs looks OK but we should ensure provenance for the patched rke2 unit. Also request explicit KMS key reference in docs for customers encrypting bundle artifacts."
  - Author: "Added a provenance.txt for the patched unit and a KMS integration note in the docs. Rolling out a follow-up to fully automate provenance signing (ENG-7890)."
- Connor Lee (QA): "Please add smoke test to CI to run the revert path in dry-run mode and assert idempotency."
  - Author: "Added tests/installer/test_bundle_manifest.py and a dry-run revert CI step. Verified idempotency locally and in CI."

CI checks (summary):
- lint: pass
- unit-tests: pass (new installer validation tests included)
- integration-smoke: pass (lab run)
- airgap-bundle-scan: pass
- e2e-onprem: pass

Merge outcome: Squash merged to main after approvals from Miguel and Priya. No post-merge hotfixes required. Release process: tagged release redwood-private-installer@v2026.02.12-offline-almalinux9 and kickoff of release pipeline to publish vendor bundle to internal artifact store for customers to download via support flow.
